canada3.title: Forestry consortium, First Nation family heading to listening circle amid more possible Ontario court action
canada3.description: A forestry consortium that was granted an interlocutory injunction halting a blockade by a family from Matachewan First Nation, allowing it to complete tree-harvesting work in northern Ontario, will sit down in a listening circle with them in a case that may see further court action. canada3.title: New memorial marks one of Canada's deadliest — but less known — highway accidents
canada3.description: A new plaque on a roadside monument west of Swift Current, Sask. details a fiery three-vehicle accident that left 22 young men dead and eight injured on May 28, 1980. The men came from out of province to work on Canadian Pacific Railway’s “Prairie Steel Gang” track crew.

canada3.title: Palestinian death toll in Gaza tops 73,000, officials say, as Israel strikes despite ceasefire
canada3.description: The Palestinian death toll from the Israel-Hamas war has surpassed 73,000, Gaza's Health Ministry said Sunday, despite a fragile ceasefire that has been described as stalled.

canada3.title: Why some say Quebec politicians helped fuel the racism they unanimously denounced
canada3.description: In a rare move, four provincial parties denounced a gathering in Shawinigan, Que., captured in a photo, during which more than a dozen masked white nationalists held a banner that read, “I remember a white Quebec.” But some observers say the province's climate in recent decades has helped fuel this

canada3.title: Thousands gather in Geneva to protest G7 as Trump, other leaders hold summit in nearby France
canada3.description: Thousands of demonstrators converged Sunday to show their discontent against the G7 group of countries, with U.S. President Donald Trump and counterparts set to hold a summit starting a day later in nearby France.

canada3.title: Trump warns Israel and Iran not to ‘blow it’ after new strikes threaten emerging ceasefire deal
canada3.description: The Israeli military said it launched strikes on Beirut on Sunday targeting Hezbollah infrastructure, despite ongoing efforts to negotiate an end to the U.S.-Iran war. Smoke could be seen rising over the Lebanese capital.

canada3.title: He’s paddled 60 km to work on B.C.’s North Coast. This week, he’ll try to kayak from Washington to Alaska
canada3.description: Prince Rupert's Yota Kano is competing in the Race to Alaska, a more than 1,200-metre race from Port Townsend, Wash., to Ketchikan, Alaska.

canada3.title: Ottawa's online harms bill 'a miss' when it comes to regulating AI chatbots: B.C. premier
canada3.description: B.C. Premier David Eby says the federal government's newly introduced online harms bill "is a miss" when it comes to addressing AI chatbots because it doesn't require tech companies to report users' concerning interactions to police.

canada3.title: It took courage to report my sexual assault. 608 days later, everything fell apart
canada3.description: Serra Al-Katib was reluctant to report a sexual assault to police, but when she heard about another victim, she decided to come forward. She didn't realize how much the process would cost her.

canada3.title: Canada's newest destroyer carries on legacy of warship lost in 1940 tragedy
canada3.description: The first of Canada's new River-class destroyers will be named HMCS Fraser. In 1940, a previous HMCS Fraser aided in evacuating British and other Allied forces from the French coast, and later became the first Royal Canadian Navy ship to sink during the Second World War.

canada3.title: B.C. woman who survived avalanche says it was like 'being hit by a truck'
canada3.description: Hannah Hughes was backcountry skiing in Norway when she looked up to see a wall of snow barreling towards her. She now faces a long recovery from her injuries.

canada3.title: British forces intercept Russian shadow fleet tanker in the Channel
canada3.description: British armed forces intercepted a sanctioned Russian shadow fleet oil tanker in the English Channel on Sunday, leading for the first time an operation to disrupt the oil revenue ​that helps fund Russia's war in Ukraine.

canada3.title: The International Space Station is showing its age
canada3.description: The International Space Station had a proposed lifespan of 15 years, but it has far exceeded that, and it's starting to show its age. Is it time to deorbit it?

canada3.title: Just how many days do provincial politicians spend legislating? We did the math
canada3.description: Some politicians say the number of days spent in the legislature doesn't matter too much, because the most important work is done in their constituency offices. Others say less time in legislatures allows provincial and territorial governments to avoid accountability and pass flawed legislation.

canada3.title: Stoned rats get the munchies. Here's what that means for people with eating disorders, appetite loss
canada3.description: It turns out stoned rats get the munchies too. New research from the University of Calgary and Washington State University digs into the effects of cannabis on rats and humans, particularly when it comes to appetite.

canada3.title: First pickleball, now padel: Why ‘social’ sports are growing in popularity
canada3.description: While the Mexican sport padel has exploded in popularity in other parts of the world, it has struggled to gain traction in Canada — until within just the last five years. Now, it’s seeing more demand than Canada’s courts can handle.

france1.title: Donald Trump turns 80 and celebrates with UFC cage fighting on the White House lawn
france1.description: President Donald Trump turned 80 on Sunday and was set to celebrate with one of the more surreal spectacles in both sports and the nation's capital: cage fighting on the White House lawn. We discuss it with our international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert.

france1.title: The week in pictures: World Cup 2026 kicks off, the Pope visits Spain and the White House prepares for a cage fight showdown
france1.description: The Pope visits Segrada Familia during his trip to Barcelona, the 2026 football World Cup kicks off in Mexico city, and the White House prepares for its first cage fight showdown. FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.

france1.title: UK celebrates King Charles’s official birthday with Trooping the Colour
france1.description: Crowds have gathered in central London for the Trooping the Colour ceremony to mark King Charles III’s official birthday.

france1.title: Beirut strikes: 'No point' in talks if US cannot uphold 'commitments'
france1.description: Iranian chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Sunday there was "no point" in continuing peace talks with the United States after its ally Israel attacked Beirut's southern suburbs.

france1.title: Trump hosts White House cage fights amid war and political scrutiny
france1.description: Donald Trump hosts a card of seven mixed martial arts fights to be held on Sunday inside a specially built arena on the White House's South Lawn on his 80th birthday, a spectacle spotlighting his norm-defying style at a tense moment in his presidency. france1.title: Israeli military strikes Beirut suburbs in the lead-up to anticipated US-Iran deal
france1.description: The Israeli military said it launched strikes on Hezbollah targets in Beirut on Sunday despite ongoing efforts to negotiate an end to the U.S.-Iran war. Smoke could be seen rising over the Lebanese capital. We discuss the latest developments with our correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

france1.description: Morocco looked impressive in their first game against Brazil, but Vinicius managed to bring it level with a beautiful goal. france1.title: 'Must-see event', rare sumo tournament kicks off in Paris
france1.description: A 150-strong delegation, two chartered planes... More than 30 years after their last visit to France, the elite of sumo wrestling – Japan's national and sacred sport – is making a highly anticipated return to Paris for a weekend showcase.

france1.title: EU says to resume membership talks with Ukraine on Monday
france1.description: The European Union will resume membership talks with Ukraine on Monday, the bloc announced, after Hungary lifted the veto imposed by its previous pro-Russian leader.

france1.title: G7 meeting begins in France this Monday
france1.description: U.S. ​President ​Donald Trump will meet with Middle ​Eastern ‌leaders ⁠and ‌attend a working session ⁠with Ukrainian President ​Volodymyr Zelenskiy ‌during the G7 summit ‌in France ​next week, senior U.S. administration officials ​said.

france1.title: Switzerland: After rapid population growth, right-wing party supports cap vote
france1.description: Swiss voters will decide the fate of a divisive anti-immigration proposal on Sunday to cap the country's population, and another referendum on restricting access to conscientious objection to military service. France 24's John Zarocostas tells us more.

france1.title: US: New York Knicks win first NBA championship since 1973
france1.description: The New York Knicks are champions of the NBA for the first time since 1973, beating the San Antonio Spurs in five games for this title. The clincher came Saturday night in a 94-90 victory, the Knicks' fourth comeback win of the series.

france1.title: Colombia leftist candidate says ready to overhaul peace process
france1.description: Colombia's left-wing presidential hopeful Ivan Cepeda said he was open to making changes to the much-criticized peace process launched by outgoing President Gustavo Petro, his staunchest ally.

france1.title: Thousands of protesters expected in Geneva ahead of nearby G7 summit
france1.description: On the eve of the G7 summit in Evian, France, neighbouring Geneva is expecting thousands of protesters to converge on the city on Sunday, under close police surveillance, more than 20 years after the violence that marred the 2003 G8 summit. france1.title: Thousands rally in Belfast to condemn anti-immigrant rioting that followed stabbing
france1.description: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Belfast on Saturday to denounce anti-immigrant rioters who set fire to homes and cars earlier in the week after a brutal stabbing blamed on an asylum seeker.

france1.title: Swiss cast ballots on right-wing's bid to cap country's population at 10 million
france1.description: Voters in Switzerland are casting final ballots Sunday on an initiative championed by the top right-wing party to cap the rich Alpine country's population at 10 million.

france1.title: Iran: US, ​Pakistani leaders predict Sunday signing of peace framework
france1.description: U.S. and Pakistani leaders forecast a Sunday signing of a long-elusive framework agreement to end months of fighting between the United States and Iran, but Tehran cast doubt over the timing and hardline protesters in Iran voiced opposition.

france1.title: UK intercepts oil tanker from Russia's shadow fleet in English Channel
france1.description: British forces intercepted a UK-sanctioned oil tanker accused of belonging to what has been dubbed Russia's "shadow fleet" in the English Channel on Sunday, in what the country’s defence ministry called "the first UK-led operation of its kind".

france1.title: World Cup 2026: Australia stun Turkey after selection gamble pays off
france1.description: Australia defeated Turkey 2-0 on Saturday at Vancouver's BC Place Stadium thanks to a goal in each half by Nestory Irankunda and Connor Metcalfe.

france1.title: History's first influencer? Marie Antoinette still receives letters
france1.description: Two hundred and forty years after their last stay at the Château de Fontainebleau south of Paris, France's King Louis XVI and Queen Marie Antoinette are again taking centre stage there.
